title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_726
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using the Fysbis backdoor in a target network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The Fysbis backdoor is a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ELF binaries and can install itself with or without root privileges.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can SSH to `next-target` using the same credentials. Enter `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. Enter `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: Investigate the `target` host and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The suspicious service is named `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that have unusual configurations or are not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services and look for any that seem suspicious.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in the previous task is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd service files and timers to see how the service is configured to start automatically. The persistence mechanism is the `payload-transfer.timer` which runs the `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers to see how the service is configured to start automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that run the suspicious service and check their configurations.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers and look for any that seem suspicious.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Identify any file transfers or remote execution used to move between hosts from the `target` to the `next-target`.
levels.solution: Check the logs and systemd timers for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts. The script used for lateral movement is `/usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the logs and systemd timers for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts that use `rsync` or `scp` to transfer files between hosts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `cat /usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh` to inspect the script used for lateral movement.
